name: Turf War
oracle_text:
When this enchantment enters, for each player, put a contested counter on target land that player controls.
Whenever a creature deals combat damage to a player, if that player controls one or more lands with contested counters on them, that creature's controller gains control of one of those lands of their choice and untaps it.
blocked_sentences: When this enchantment enters, for each player, put a contested counter on target land that player controls.

needs.what: a target spec whose size is mandatory and set by the board: exactly one target land for EACH player who controls one (no two from the same player, nobody skipped, the caster's own seat included), so the controller must mark one of their own lands as well as one of each opponent's
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `one_per_player` is accepted only with count 'any', a ceiling (count N with up_to) or a literal count of 2 or more (cards/loader/targets.py), so it says 'up to one target land per player' and lets the caster skip their own land -- the card's whole drawback -- or a literal 2 that is wrong in any pod that is not two players; a computed exact count is refused by the loader. A for_each_player with a non-targeting choice would dodge hexproof/shroud and is not 'target'. The second sentence looks expressible: a deals_combat_damage_to_player trigger with an `exists` condition over lands with has_counters 'contested' controlled by {binding: event_player}, then gain_control with player {controller_of: subject}, a count-1 selector with chooser {controller_of: subject} and `as`, then untap of that binding
